## 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE

OZEMPIC is indicated:

- •
excerpt.match: as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

•

- • to reduce the risk of sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, and cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease.

comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff asked why Lilly excluded upfront payments for acquired IPR&D (asset deals and licenses) from non-GAAP when they look like normal recurring cash operating expenses.
comment_letters.company_answer: Lilly argued at length the charges were unpredictable 'buy-in' investments, then after calls agreed that from Q1 2022 non-GAAP would include acquired IPR&D upfronts and development milestones, recasting prior periods.
comment_letters.next_filing_disclosure: FY2022 10-K highlights acquired IPR&D and development milestones of $908.5M (2022) and $970.1M (2021); from 2022 these are no longer adjusted out of non-GAAP EPS.
comment_letters.why_it_matters: Lilly's own letter warned it might stop giving non-GAAP guidance without the adjustment; the change lowers adjusted EPS by every BD deal and matters to any EPS-based bonus (see incentive_metrics).
comment_letters.impact_estimate: Acquired IPR&D in non-GAAP: 2018 $1.98B, 2019 $0.24B, 2020 $0.66B, 9M 2021 $0.50B (reply table); 2021 full year $970M ~ $1.07/share pre-tax at ~0.9B shares.
comment_letters.staff_quote: For each type of acquired IPR&D transaction (i.e., asset acquisitions, license agreements, etc.), explain to us why you believe it is appropriate to include non- GAAP adjustments for these upfront payments given that these expenditures appear to be normal, recurring, cash operating expenses necessary to operate your business.
comment_letters.reply_quote: In response to the Staff's comment and as discussed with the Staff, beginning with Lilly's earnings release for the quarter ended March 31, 2022, Lilly will not include adjustments for upfront charges and developmental milestones related to acquired in-process research and development projects acquired in a transaction other than a business combination in presentations of its non-GAAP measures.

comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff asked why the 10-K had less climate detail than Lilly's ESG and CDP reports, and pressed three rounds for weather damages, water risk, insurance cost and carbon credits.
comment_letters.company_answer: Lilly said none was material: no tracked weather loss events of $100,000 or more in 2020-2022, property insurance about 0.08% of costs, and no change to the filing.
comment_letters.next_filing_disclosure: No new 10-K disclosure committed beyond 'will continue to evaluate'.
comment_letters.why_it_matters: Low case value: the ESG-vs-filing gap was closed by immaterial numbers, no hidden economics.
comment_letters.impact_estimate: Immaterial per company (property insurance 0.078% / 0.077% / ~0.08% of COGS+opex 2020-2022).
comment_letters.staff_quote: We note that you provided more expansive disclosure in your 2022 ESG Report, CDP 2022 Climate response and 2022 CDP Water Security response than you provided in your SEC filings.
comment_letters.reply_quote: For each of the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021 and 2020, there were no tracked damage or loss events affecting our property and operations from weather related events that met or exceeded that threshold.

comment_letters.filing_reviewed: Elanco S-4 / Lilly Schedule TO-I (Elanco split-off exchange offer)
comment_letters.staff_ask: Staff asked whether Lilly should quantify the 'material adverse change in stock price' termination condition in the Elanco exchange offer.
comment_letters.company_answer: Lilly's counsel defended the pricing mechanism by analogy to the CBS-Entercom exchange offer.
comment_letters.staff_quote: Disclosure on page 86 indicates that Lilly may terminate the exchange offer if there occurs, or Lilly reasonably expects there may occur, a material adverse change in the stock price of Elanco or the stock price of Lilly.

memo_points.text: Jardiance revenue has carried a growing one-off every year (a $300M amendment payment in 2024, $570M in 2025, up to $910M of milestones limited to 2026, $500M already booked in H1), and the FY2025 10-K newly states that its most significant markets leave the Boehringer collaboration after December 31, 2028. Impact: nugget dRev (bull, base, bear) (500, 910, 910) x CM 1.00 x (1 - t 0.2049) / D 893.7 (line revenue; estimate from nugget LLY-nugget-002).

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge that opened Zepbound and Foundayo to seniors at $245 ends December 31, 2027 and exists only because Part D plans declined to opt in ('we now know they didn't'), while 30% to 40% of Bridge patients are not new, so part of the 'new access' is existing patients moving from about $346 self-pay to $245. Impact: nugget dRev (bull, base, bear) (61, 242, 485) x CM 1.00 x (1 - t 0.2049) / D 893.7 (line revenue; estimate from nugget LLY-nugget-005).

Verzenio is already shrinking in the US (Q2 2026 -9%) and now faces two clocks at once: a Medicare set price from January 2028 and a Cipla patent challenge filed in March 2026; Pfizer's rival Ibrance got a set price about 49% below its Part D cost per claim. Impact: nugget dRev (bull, base, bear) (317, 519, 634) x CM 0.70 x (1 - t 0.2049) / D 893.7 (line revenue; estimate from nugget LLY-nugget-006).

questions.q: Which of the three forces hits Eli Lilly hardest?
